headline: AI could help combat the global fatty liver epidemic affecting 1 billion people
summary: Artificial intelligence is being explored to analyze health records and identify individuals at high risk for fatty liver disease, which impacts 30% of adults worldwide and often goes undetected.
details: A silent epidemic of fatty liver disease is affecting over a billion people globally, with fat accumulation exceeding 5-10% of liver weight in many individuals. This condition causes inflammation, fibrosis, and can lead to liver failure, cardiovascular disease, and cancer, often without early symptoms.

Specialists are investigating how AI can help by sifting through vast electronic health records to pinpoint those most at risk of developing significant liver fat. This proactive approach aims to shift focus from late-stage care to early detection and prevention.

Early identification of fatty liver disease can make much of the damage reversible through lifestyle changes like diet, exercise, and reduced alcohol intake. Even advanced scarring can be treated with novel medications.

Despite the existence of simple, noninvasive assessments like the Fib-4 index, they are underutilized. AI could automate the calculation of these scores using routine blood test data, making it easier for primary care physicians to identify patients needing specialist referral.

Furthermore, AI models are being trained to analyze routine chest X-rays, which incidentally capture parts of the liver. One study showed an AI model identifying fatty liver disease with 82% accuracy from these scans.
caption:
A global epidemic of fatty liver disease affects over 1 billion people, often going undetected until it's life-threatening. AI is emerging as a potential tool for early identification.

headline: Codex Desktop for Linux is now available, bringing agentic coding to developers
summary: Powered by OpenAI's frontier coding models, Codex in ChatGPT acts as a command center for agentic coding, handling complex tasks and routine work across projects.
details: OpenAI's Codex Desktop for Linux is now available, bringing advanced agentic coding capabilities directly to developers. Powered by OpenAI's frontier coding models, Codex is designed to reliably complete end-to-end tasks like building features, complex refactors, and migrations.

Operating as a command center within ChatGPT, Codex leverages built-in worktrees and cloud environments. This allows agents to work in parallel across multiple projects, significantly accelerating development cycles from weeks to days.

The platform introduces "Skills," enabling teams to teach Codex their specific standards, workflows, and operational methods. Codex then applies these consistently across all tasks, enhancing its contribution effectiveness with minimal supervision.

Developers can schedule Codex to manage routine yet crucial work, including issue triage, alert monitoring, and CI/CD processes. This automation frees up engineering teams to concentrate on core system design and high-leverage decision-making.

Codex also aims to elevate baseline code quality through more thorough designs, comprehensive testing, and high-signal code reviews. This proactive approach helps catch issues early, boosting team confidence in shipping robust software.

The tool offers versatile integration, accessible across ChatGPT, various code editors, and the terminal, all seamlessly connected via a user's ChatGPT account. This ensures a unified and efficient developer experience.
Early adopters report substantial productivity gains; for instance, one team cut early iteration time by 30-50%, while another stated they now "ship in a weekend what previously took a quarter."
